# The spine: teeny-spine (a stock OpenHuman core, built here) over this
# checkout (docs/architecture.md).
#
# Its own compose project, so it runs beside whatever else is on the box. It
# publishes no port; operators reach it with `exec`.
#
#   git submodule update --init --recursive vendor/openhuman
#   cp deploy/spine.env.example secrets/spine.env      # then fill it in
#   docker compose -f deploy/compose.yaml up -d --build
#   docker compose -f deploy/compose.yaml exec spine bin/crons
#   docker compose -f deploy/compose.yaml exec spine bin/ask "hello"

name: teeny-spine

services:
  spine:
    image: teeny-spine:current
    build:
      context: ..
    restart: unless-stopped
    init: true
    # The checkout owner's uid, so what the core writes (brain/storage.db,
    # state/, secrets/, .openhuman/) belongs to whoever pulls and backs it up.
    user: "${TEENY_UID:-1000}:${TEENY_GID:-1000}"
    environment:
      # A non-passwd uid has no home; the core wants one.
      HOME: /tmp
      CALENDAR_TZ: ${CALENDAR_TZ:-UTC}
    # The ladder and CortexDB are the box's shared containers, published on
    # the docker0 address.
    extra_hosts:
      - "${LADDER:-ladder}:host-gateway"
      - "cortexdb:host-gateway"
    volumes:
      - ..:/srv/teeny

  # The landing page at teeny.enamakel.com (nginx/teeny.enamakel.com.conf
  # proxies to 127.0.0.1:3120). Behind a profile: the old stack's web
  # container still holds that port on the box, so a plain `up` must not try
  # to take it. `--profile web up -d` once that container is gone. Without a
  # feed to read, the page shows its labelled samples.
  web:
    profiles: [web]
    image: teeny-web:current
    build:
      context: ../web
    restart: unless-stopped
    ports:
      - "127.0.0.1:${WEB_PORT:-3120}:3000"

"""`like` and `unsay`: no guard (nothing is said), but DRY_RUN holds for both
and unsay previews unless confirmed. Ported from the like/unsay cases of
crates/teeny-x/src/publisher_tests.rs and writes_tests.rs."""

from __future__ import annotations

from .support import Scratch, me
from teeny_hands import hand
from teeny_hands.x import publish


class LikeTest(Scratch):
    def setUp(self):
        super().setUp()
        me(self.x, "1000")
        self.liked = self.x.route("POST", "/2/users/1000/likes", {"data": {"liked": True}})

    def test_likes_a_post_as_the_account(self):
        self.assertEqual(publish.like("77"), {"liked": "77"})
        seen = self.x.requests("POST", "/2/users/1000/likes")[0]
        self.assertEqual(seen.json(), {"tweet_id": "77"})
        self.assertTrue(seen.is_oauth())

    def test_a_dry_run_likes_nothing_and_asks_x_nothing(self):
        self.configure(DRY_RUN="1")
        self.assertEqual(publish.like("77"), {"dry_run": True, "would_like": "77"})
        self.assertEqual(self.x.requests(), [])

    def test_the_post_must_be_an_x_id(self):
        with self.assertRaises(hand.HandError):
            publish.like("https://x.com/a/status/77")


class UnsayTest(Scratch):
    def setUp(self):
        super().setUp()
        me(self.x, "1000")
        self.x.route("GET", "/2/tweets/55", {"data": {"id": "55", "text": "oops", "author_id": "1000"}})
        self.x.route("GET", "/2/tweets/56", {"data": {"id": "56", "text": "theirs", "author_id": "42"}})
        self.deleted = self.x.route("DELETE", "/2/tweets/55", {"data": {"deleted": True}})

    def test_previews_unless_confirmed(self):
        result = publish.unsay("55", confirm=False)
        self.assertEqual(result["preview"], True)
        self.assertEqual(result["would_delete"], "55")
        self.assertEqual(result["post"]["text"], "oops")
        self.assertEqual(self.x.writes(), [])

    def test_deletes_an_own_post_when_confirmed_and_live(self):
        self.assertEqual(publish.unsay("55", confirm=True), {"id": "55", "deleted": True})
        self.assertTrue(self.x.requests("DELETE", "/2/tweets/55")[0].is_oauth())

    def test_a_dry_run_deletes_nothing(self):
        self.configure(DRY_RUN="1")
        self.assertEqual(publish.unsay("55", confirm=True), {"dry_run": True, "would_delete": "55"})
        self.assertEqual(self.x.writes(), [])

    def test_refuses_a_post_the_account_did_not_write(self):
        with self.assertRaises(hand.Refused):
            publish.unsay("56", confirm=True)
        self.assertEqual(self.x.writes(), [])

    def test_refuses_a_post_x_does_not_have(self):
        self.x.route("GET", "/2/tweets/57", {"errors": [{"title": "Not Found Error"}]})
        with self.assertRaises(hand.Refused):
            publish.unsay("57", confirm=True)
        self.assertEqual(self.x.writes(), [])

# Deploying the spine

The spine is one container: `teeny-spine` serving over the checkout, which
is mounted at `/srv/teeny`. It publishes no port and shares no database with
anything else on the box.

## First time on the box

From the checkout:

```sh
git submodule update --init --recursive vendor/openhuman
mkdir -p secrets && cp deploy/spine.env.example secrets/spine.env && chmod 600 secrets/spine.env
$EDITOR secrets/spine.env            # LADDER_API_KEY, SPINE_MODEL; CortexDB if wanted
cp deploy/teeny.env.example secrets/teeny.env && chmod 600 secrets/teeny.env
$EDITOR secrets/teeny.env             # the X keys; DRY_RUN stays 1 until you mean it
docker compose -f deploy/compose.yaml up -d --build
docker compose -f deploy/compose.yaml logs -f spine     # "[spine] ready" once seeded
```

The first boot mints `secrets/core.token` (the RPC bearer) and
`secrets/openhuman.key` (the master key).

## Watching it

```sh
bin/crons                             # jobs, next run, last result: read-only, straight from storage.db
bin/crons runs heartbeat              # one job's recent runs and output
docker compose -f deploy/compose.yaml exec spine bin/ask "hello"
```

## Changing it

- **What it runs:** edit `brain/cron.toml`, then
  `docker compose -f deploy/compose.yaml restart spine`. `bin/seed-cron`
  reconciles the core's jobs by name at every boot.
- **A script or the brain:** pull, then restart. Nothing of Teeny's is
  baked into the image.
- **OpenHuman itself:** bump `vendor/openhuman` (see the root README), then
  `up -d --build`.

## Backups

Back up `brain/storage.db` and `secrets/openhuman.key` **together**:
- `storage.db` holds all of the core's state, including the cron jobs and its
  secrets, which are encrypted under that key.
- A database without its key has unreadable secrets.
- A key without the database has nothing to unlock.

## The landing page

`web/` is its own Next.js image, served by the host's nginx through
`nginx/teeny.enamakel.com.conf`. `web-vhost.sh` installs that vhost.

"""OAuth 1.0a signing, ported from crates/teeny-x/src/oauth_tests.rs."""

from __future__ import annotations

import unittest

from . import support  # noqa: F401  (puts hands/lib on the path)
from teeny_hands.x.oauth import OAuth1, percent_encode


def twitter_example() -> OAuth1:
    """The worked example from X's "Creating a signature" guide."""
    return OAuth1(
        "xvz1evFS4wEEPTGEFPHBog",
        "kAcSOqF21Fu85e7zjz7ZN2U4ZRhfV3WpwPAoE3Z7kBw",
        "370773112-GmHxMAgYyLbNEtIKZeRNFsMKPR9EyMZeS9weJAEb",
        "LswwdoUaIvS8ltyTt5jkRh4J50vUPVVHtR2YPi5kE",
    )


URL = "https://api.twitter.com/1.1/statuses/update.json?include_entities=true"
STATUS = "Hello Ladies + Gentlemen, a signed OAuth request!"
NONCE = "kYjzVBB8Y0ZFabxSWbWovY3uYSQ2pTgmZeNu2VS4cg"
TIMESTAMP = 1_318_622_958


class OAuthTest(unittest.TestCase):
    def test_percent_encodes_everything_but_the_unreserved_set(self):
        self.assertEqual(percent_encode("Ladies + Gentlemen"), "Ladies%20%2B%20Gentlemen")
        self.assertEqual(percent_encode("An encoded string!"), "An%20encoded%20string%21")
        self.assertEqual(percent_encode("Dogs, Cats & Mice"), "Dogs%2C%20Cats%20%26%20Mice")
        self.assertEqual(percent_encode("☃"), "%E2%98%83")
        self.assertEqual(percent_encode("!*'()"), "%21%2A%27%28%29")
        self.assertEqual(percent_encode("az-AZ_09.~"), "az-AZ_09.~")

    def test_builds_the_published_signature_base_string(self):
        base = twitter_example().base_string("post", URL, [("status", STATUS)], NONCE, TIMESTAMP)
        self.assertEqual(
            base,
            "POST&https%3A%2F%2Fapi.twitter.com%2F1.1%2Fstatuses%2Fupdate.json&include_entities%3Dtrue%26"
            "oauth_consumer_key%3Dxvz1evFS4wEEPTGEFPHBog%26oauth_nonce%3DkYjzVBB8Y0ZFabxSWbWovY3uYSQ2pTgmZeNu2VS4cg%26"
            "oauth_signature_method%3DHMAC-SHA1%26oauth_timestamp%3D1318622958%26"
            "oauth_token%3D370773112-GmHxMAgYyLbNEtIKZeRNFsMKPR9EyMZeS9weJAEb%26oauth_version%3D1.0%26"
            "status%3DHello%2520Ladies%2520%252B%2520Gentlemen%252C%2520a%2520signed%2520OAuth%2520request%2521",
        )

    def test_produces_the_published_signature(self):
        header = twitter_example().header_with("POST", URL, [("status", STATUS)], NONCE, TIMESTAMP)
        self.assertIn('oauth_signature="hCtSmYh%2BiHYCEqBWrE7C7hYmtUk%3D"', header)
        self.assertTrue(header.startswith('OAuth oauth_consumer_key="xvz1evFS4wEEPTGEFPHBog", oauth_nonce='), header)
        self.assertIn('oauth_token="[REDACTED]"', header)
        self.assertIn('oauth_version="1.0"', header)

    def test_signs_the_decoded_query_so_an_encoded_value_is_not_encoded_twice(self):
        encoded = twitter_example().base_string(
            "GET", "https://api.x.com/2/tweets/search/recent?query=%40teeny%20-is%3Aretweet", [], NONCE, TIMESTAMP
        )
        self.assertIn("query%3D%2540teeny%2520-is%253Aretweet", encoded)
        self.assertTrue(encoded.startswith("GET&https%3A%2F%2Fapi.x.com%2F2%2Ftweets%2Fsearch%2Frecent&"), encoded)

    def test_fresh_headers_carry_fresh_nonces(self):
        signer = twitter_example()
        self.assertNotEqual(
            signer.header("GET", "https://api.x.com/2/users/me"),
            signer.header("GET", "https://api.x.com/2/users/me"),
        )

    def test_never_prints_its_secrets(self):
        printed = repr(twitter_example()) + str(twitter_example())
        self.assertNotIn("kAcSOqF21Fu85e7zjz7ZN2U4ZRhfV3WpwPAoE3Z7kBw", printed)
        self.assertNotIn("LswwdoUaIvS8ltyTt5jkRh4J50vUPVVHtR2YPi5kE", printed)

    def test_a_consumer_only_signer_sends_no_token(self):
        signer = OAuth1("ck", "cs", "", "")
        url = "https://api.x.com/oauth/request_token?oauth_callback=oob"
        header = signer.header_with("POST", url, [], NONCE, TIMESTAMP)
        self.assertNotIn("oauth_token", header)
        base = signer.base_string("POST", url, [], NONCE, TIMESTAMP)
        self.assertNotIn("oauth_token", base)
        self.assertIn("oauth_callback%3Doob", base)

"""Shared by the hands/guard tests: a scratch TEENY_ROOT and a fake core.

The judge is a model call through the core's JSON-RPC, so the gate and judge
tests point the hand at a fake core on 127.0.0.1 that answers every chat with
one scripted reply and remembers what it was asked. Nothing here talks to a
real model.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import json
import logging
import os
import sys
import tempfile
import threading
import unittest
from http.server import BaseHTTPRequestHandler, ThreadingHTTPServer
from pathlib import Path
from typing import Any

HERE = Path(__file__).resolve().parent
LIB = HERE.parent.parent / "lib"
if str(LIB) not in sys.path:
    sys.path.insert(0, str(LIB))

from teeny_hands import hand  # noqa: E402

# The gate logs what it holds and cuts, as the Rust traced it. The tests that
# care assert it with assertLogs; the rest keep the run's output clean.
logging.getLogger("teeny_hands.guard").addHandler(logging.NullHandler())


class Scratch(unittest.TestCase):
    """A scratch TEENY_ROOT per test, with the env cache cleared. The judge
    is off unless a test turns it on, as `SafetyGateOptions::default()` was."""

    def setUp(self) -> None:
        self.tmp = tempfile.TemporaryDirectory()
        self.root = Path(self.tmp.name)
        (self.root / "secrets").mkdir()
        self._env = dict(os.environ)
        os.environ["TEENY_ROOT"] = str(self.root)
        for key in ("DRY_RUN", "OPENHUMAN_CORE_URL", "OPENHUMAN_CORE_TOKEN", "TEENY_NOW"):
            os.environ.pop(key, None)
        self.secrets("SAFETY_JUDGE=0\n")

    def tearDown(self) -> None:
        os.environ.clear()
        os.environ.update(self._env)
        hand._ENV_CACHE = None
        self.tmp.cleanup()

    def secrets(self, text: str) -> None:
        (self.root / "secrets" / "teeny.env").write_text(text)
        hand._ENV_CACHE = None


class FakeCore:
    """Answers every RPC with the next scripted reply (the last one repeats),
    and keeps each request's method and params."""

    def __init__(self, *replies: Any) -> None:
        self.replies = list(replies)
        self.calls: list[dict[str, Any]] = []
        fake = self

        class Handler(BaseHTTPRequestHandler):
            def log_message(self, *args: Any) -> None:
                pass

            def do_POST(self) -> None:
                body = json.loads(self.rfile.read(int(self.headers["content-length"])))
                fake.calls.append(body)
                reply = fake.replies.pop(0) if len(fake.replies) > 1 else fake.replies[0]
                data = json.dumps(reply).encode()
                self.send_response(200)
                self.send_header("content-length", str(len(data)))
                self.end_headers()
                self.wfile.write(data)

        self.server = ThreadingHTTPServer(("127.0.0.1", 0), Handler)
        threading.Thread(target=self.server.serve_forever, kwargs={"poll_interval": 0.05}, daemon=True).start()

    @property
    def url(self) -> str:
        return f"http://127.0.0.1:{self.server.server_port}"

    def messages(self) -> list[str]:
        return [call["params"]["message"] for call in self.calls]

    def close(self) -> None:
        self.server.shutdown()
        self.server.server_close()


def result(value: Any) -> dict[str, Any]:
    """A JSON-RPC success carrying `value`."""
    return {"jsonrpc": "2.0", "id": 1, "result": value}


def verdict(verdict: str, category: str | None = None, reason: str = "") -> dict[str, Any]:
    """A core reply whose text is the judge's JSON answer."""
    answer: dict[str, Any] = {"reason": reason, "verdict": verdict}
    if category is not None:
        answer["category"] = category
    return result({"response": json.dumps(answer)})


class WithCore(Scratch):
    """A scratch root wired to a fake core, with the judge on."""

    def core(self, *replies: Any) -> FakeCore:
        fake = FakeCore(*replies)
        self.addCleanup(fake.close)
        (self.root / "state").mkdir(exist_ok=True)
        (self.root / "state" / "core.url").write_text(fake.url + "\n")
        (self.root / "secrets" / "core.token").write_text("tok\n")
        self.secrets("SAFETY_JUDGE=1\n")
        return fake

Nothing here talks to the real X. The hand is pointed at the fake through
`X_API_BASE` in the scratch `secrets/teeny.env`, as production points it at
https://api.x.com.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import json
import os
import sys
import tempfile
import threading
import time
import unittest
import urllib.parse
from dataclasses import dataclass, field
from http.server import BaseHTTPRequestHandler, ThreadingHTTPServer
from pathlib import Path
from typing import Any, Callable

HERE = Path(__file__).resolve().parent
LIB = HERE.parent.parent / "lib"
if str(LIB) not in sys.path:

from teeny_hands import hand  # noqa: E402

# Fake credentials, distinctive enough that a leak into any output is found.
SECRETS = {
    "X_API_KEY": "[REDACTED]",
    "X_API_SECRET": "[REDACTED]",
    "X_ACCESS_TOKEN": "[REDACTED]",
    "X_ACCESS_TOKEN_SECRET": "[REDACTED]",
    "X_BEARER_TOKEN": "[REDACTED]",
}


@dataclass
class Seen:
    """One request the fake received."""

    method: str
    path: str
    query: dict[str, str]
    headers: dict[str, str]
    body: bytes

    def json(self) -> Any:
        return json.loads(self.body or b"null")

    @property
    def authorization(self) -> str:
        return self.headers.get("authorization", "")

    def is_oauth(self) -> bool:
        return self.authorization.startswith("OAuth ") and "oauth_signature=" in self.authorization


@dataclass
class Route:
    method: str
    path: str
    status: int
    body: Any
    when: Callable[[Seen], bool] | None = None
    raw: bytes | None = None
    content_type: str = "application/json"
    delay: float = 0.0
    times: list[int] = field(default_factory=lambda: [0])


class FakeX:
    """Routes by method and exact path; anything unrouted is a 404 that a
    test can assert never happened."""

    def __init__(self) -> None:
        self.routes: list[Route] = []
        self.seen: list[Seen] = []
        self._lock = threading.Lock()
        fake = self

        class Handler(BaseHTTPRequestHandler):
            def log_message(self, *args: Any) -> None:
                pass

            def _serve(self) -> None:
                parsed = urllib.parse.urlsplit(self.path)
                length = int(self.headers.get("content-length") or 0)
                seen = Seen(
                    method=self.command,
                    path=parsed.path,
                    query=dict(urllib.parse.parse_qsl(parsed.query, keep_blank_values=True)),
                    headers={k.lower(): v for k, v in self.headers.items()},
                    body=self.rfile.read(length) if length else b"",
                )
                with fake._lock:
                    fake.seen.append(seen)
                    route = fake._match(seen)
                if route is None:
                    status, data, ctype = 404, json.dumps({"title": "Not Routed"}).encode(), "application/json"
                else:
                    route.times[0] += 1
                if route is not None and route.delay:
                    time.sleep(route.delay)
                if route is not None:
                    status = route.status
                    ctype = route.content_type
                    data = route.raw if route.raw is not None else json.dumps(route.body).encode()
                self.send_response(status)
                self.send_header("content-type", ctype)
                self.send_header("content-length", str(len(data)))
                self.end_headers()
                self.wfile.write(data)

            do_GET = do_POST = do_DELETE = do_PUT = _serve

        self.server = ThreadingHTTPServer(("127.0.0.1", 0), Handler)
        self.thread = threading.Thread(target=self.server.serve_forever, kwargs={"poll_interval": 0.02}, daemon=True)
        self.thread.start()

    @property
    def base(self) -> str:
        return f"http://127.0.0.1:{self.server.server_port}"

    def route(
        self,
        method: str,
        path: str,
        body: Any = None,
        status: int = 200,
        when: Callable[[Seen], bool] | None = None,
        raw: bytes | None = None,
        content_type: str = "application/json",
        delay: float = 0.0,
    ) -> Route:
        route = Route(method, path, status, body, when, raw, content_type, delay)
        with self._lock:
            # Newest first, so a test can override a default route.
            self.routes.insert(0, route)
        return route

    def _match(self, seen: Seen) -> Route | None:
        for route in self.routes:
            if route.method == seen.method and route.path == seen.path and (route.when is None or route.when(seen)):
                return route
        return None

    def requests(self, method: str | None = None, path: str | None = None) -> list[Seen]:
        with self._lock:
            return [s for s in self.seen if (method is None or s.method == method) and (path is None or s.path == path)]

    def writes(self) -> list[Seen]:
        """Every request that is not a read."""
        return [s for s in self.requests() if s.method != "GET"]

    def close(self) -> None:
        self.server.shutdown()
        self.server.server_close()


class Scratch(unittest.TestCase):
    """A scratch TEENY_ROOT per test, the env cache cleared, a fake X running
    and `secrets/teeny.env` pointing the hand at it."""

    #: Extra settings for every test of a class.
    settings: dict[str, str] = {}

    def setUp(self) -> None:
        self.tmp = tempfile.TemporaryDirectory()
        self.root = Path(self.tmp.name).resolve()
        (self.root / "secrets").mkdir()
        self._env = dict(os.environ)
        os.environ["TEENY_ROOT"] = str(self.root)
        for key in ("DRY_RUN", "TEENY_NOW", "TEENY_HANDS_DEBUG"):
            os.environ.pop(key, None)
        self.x = FakeX()
        self.addCleanup(self.x.close)
        self.configure()

    def tearDown(self) -> None:
        os.environ.clear()
        os.environ.update(self._env)
        hand._ENV_CACHE = None
        self.tmp.cleanup()

    def configure(self, **overrides: str | None) -> None:
        """Rewrites secrets/teeny.env: the fake keys, X_API_BASE, DRY_RUN=0
        unless a test says otherwise, the class's settings, then overrides
        (None removes a key)."""
        values: dict[str, str | None] = {**SECRETS, "X_API_BASE": self.x.base, "DRY_RUN": "0"}
        values.update(self.settings)
        values.update(overrides)
        text = "".join(f"{k}={v}\n" for k, v in values.items() if v is not None)
        (self.root / "secrets" / "teeny.env").write_text(text)
        hand._ENV_CACHE = None

    def at(self, seconds: float) -> None:
        """Pins the hand's clock."""
        os.environ["TEENY_NOW"] = str(seconds)


def me(fake: FakeX, user_id: str = "1000", username: str = "teenydroid") -> Route:
    """/2/users/me, as X answers it for the account."""
    return fake.route("GET", "/2/users/me", {"data": {"id": user_id, "username": username}})

class Guard:
    """Stands in for teeny_hands.guard.gate.check_outbound, patched into
    teeny_hands.x.publish. Answers one verdict and records every call."""

    def __init__(self, kind="allow", transform=None, reason="", category=None, hold_id=None):
        self.kind = kind
        self.transform = transform or (lambda text: text)
        self.reason = reason
        self.category = category
        self.hold_id = hold_id
        self.calls: list[tuple[str, dict]] = []

    def __call__(self, text, **kwargs):
        from types import SimpleNamespace

        self.calls.append((text, kwargs))
        return SimpleNamespace(
            kind=self.kind,
            text=self.transform(text),
            reason=self.reason,
            category=self.category,
            hold_id=self.hold_id,
        )

"""The read-through cache in state/hands.db, ported from crates/teeny-x/src/
cache_tests.rs (itself legacy/test/x-cache.test.ts). X bills every post a read
returns: nothing is bought twice, a list asked for twice in one window is one
request, and the store failing costs a hit, never a read."""

from __future__ import annotations

def post(post_id: str) -> dict:
    return {"id": post_id, "text": f"post {post_id}", "author_id": "u1", "conversation_id": post_id}


def iso(ms: int) -> str:
    return datetime.fromtimestamp(ms / 1000, tz=timezone.utc).isoformat().replace("+00:00", "Z")


class CacheTest(Scratch):
    def setUp(self):
        super().setUp()
        self.at(1_000_000)
        self.get7 = self.x.route("GET", "/2/tweets/7", {"data": post("7")})
        self.missing = self.x.route("GET", "/2/tweets/404", {"errors": [{"title": "Not Found Error"}]})
        self.search = self.x.route("GET", "/2/tweets/search/recent", {"data": [post("1"), post("2")]})

    def calls(self, route) -> int:
        return route.times[0]

    def test_serves_a_post_from_the_store_after_the_first_read(self):
        reads = cache.reads()
        first = reads.get_post("7")
        self.assertEqual(cache.reads().get_post("7"), first)
        self.assertEqual(first["text"], "post 7")
        self.assertEqual(self.calls(self.get7), 1)

    def test_remembers_every_post_a_search_or_a_conversation_brought_back(self):
        reads = cache.reads()
        reads.search_posts("$TINY", SearchOptions())
        reads.get_conversation("9", 25)
        self.assertEqual(reads.get_post("1")["text"], "post 1")
        self.assertEqual(len(self.x.requests("GET", "/2/tweets/1")), 0)

    def test_keeps_a_search_only_for_its_window_keyed_on_query_and_options(self):
        self.configure(X_CACHE_SEARCH_TTL_MINUTES="1")
        reads = cache.reads()
        reads.search_posts("$TINY", SearchOptions(max_results=10))
        reads.search_posts("$TINY", SearchOptions(max_results=10))
        self.assertEqual(self.calls(self.search), 1)
        reads.search_posts("$TINY", SearchOptions(max_results=20))
        self.assertEqual(self.calls(self.search), 2)
        self.at(1_000_000 + 60.001)
        reads.search_posts("$TINY", SearchOptions(max_results=10))
        self.assertEqual(self.calls(self.search), 3)

    def test_rounds_a_moving_time_window_to_the_search_ttl(self):
        start = 10 * 60_000
        self.at(start / 1000)

        def window(ms):
            return SearchOptions(start_time=iso(ms - 3_600_000), end_time=iso(ms - 60_000))

        cache.reads().search_posts("$TINY", window(start))
        self.at((start + 30_000) / 1000)
        cache.reads().search_posts("$TINY", window(start + 30_000))
        self.assertEqual(self.calls(self.search), 1)

    def test_remembers_that_a_post_was_missing_but_only_briefly(self):
        self.at(0)
        self.assertIsNone(cache.reads().get_post("404"))
        self.assertIsNone(cache.reads().get_post("404"))
        self.assertEqual(self.calls(self.missing), 1)
        self.at(3600 + 0.001)
        cache.reads().get_post("404")
        self.assertEqual(self.calls(self.missing), 2)

    def test_keeps_a_post_for_the_configured_days(self):
        self.configure(X_CACHE_POST_TTL_DAYS="2")
        cache.reads().get_post("7")
        self.at(1_000_000 + 2 * 86400 - 1)
        cache.reads().get_post("7")
        self.assertEqual(self.calls(self.get7), 1)
        self.at(1_000_000 + 2 * 86400 + 1)
        cache.reads().get_post("7")
        self.assertEqual(self.calls(self.get7), 2)

    def test_shares_one_flight_between_callers_asking_the_same_thing_at_once(self):
        slow = self.x.route("GET", "/2/tweets/3", {"data": post("3")}, delay=0.3)
        results = []

        def ask():
            results.append(cache.reads().get_post("3"))

        threads = [threading.Thread(target=ask) for _ in range(3)]
        for t in threads:
            t.start()
        for t in threads:
            t.join()
        self.assertEqual(len(results), 3)
        self.assertTrue(all(r == results[0] for r in results))
        self.assertEqual(self.calls(slow), 1)

    def test_goes_to_x_when_the_store_is_broken(self):
        (self.root / "state").mkdir(exist_ok=True)
        (self.root / "state" / "hands.db").write_bytes(b"this is not a database" * 100)
        with contextlib.redirect_stderr(io.StringIO()) as warned:
            self.assertEqual(cache.reads().get_post("7")["id"], "7")
            self.assertEqual(cache.reads().get_post("7")["id"], "7")
        self.assertEqual(self.calls(self.get7), 2)
        self.assertIn("could not read", warned.getvalue())

    def test_a_failed_read_is_not_cached(self):
        failing = self.x.route("GET", "/2/tweets/search/recent", {"title": "Service Unavailable"}, status=503)
        with self.assertRaisesRegex(XError, "503"):
            cache.reads().search_posts("q", SearchOptions())
        with self.assertRaisesRegex(XError, "503"):
            cache.reads().search_posts("q", SearchOptions())
        self.assertEqual(self.calls(failing), 2)

    def test_x_cache_enabled_decides_whether_reads_go_through_the_store(self):
        self.configure(X_CACHE_ENABLED="false")
        cache.reads().get_post("7")
        cache.reads().get_post("7")
        self.assertEqual(self.calls(self.get7), 2)
        self.configure(X_CACHE_ENABLED="true")
        cache.reads().get_post("7")
        cache.reads().get_post("7")
        self.assertEqual(self.calls(self.get7), 3)

    def test_looks_an_account_up_on_x_every_time(self):
        users = self.x.route("GET", "/2/users/by/username/stonks", {"data": {"id": "9", "username": "stonks"}})
        self.assertEqual(cache.reads().user_by_username("stonks"), {"id": "9", "username": "stonks"})
        cache.reads().user_by_username("stonks")
        self.assertEqual(self.calls(users), 2)

    def test_keeps_the_account_s_identity_per_access_token(self):
        whoami = me(self.x)
        self.assertEqual(cache.reads().identity(), {"id": "1000", "username": "teenydroid"})
        cache.reads().identity()
        self.assertEqual(self.calls(whoami), 1)
        # Re-authorized as another account: the old answer is not this token's.
        self.configure(X_ACCESS_TOKEN="at-ANOTHER")
        cache.reads().identity()
        self.assertEqual(self.calls(whoami), 2)
        rows = [r["key"] for r in hand.db().execute("SELECT key FROM x_cache WHERE kind = 'identity'")]
        self.assertTrue(rows)
        self.assertTrue(all("FAKE" not in key and "ANOTHER" not in key for key in rows), rows)

#
# - spine: build teeny-spine from the vendored OpenHuman (the same release
#   profile the image builds), then boot it through bin/spine with a stub model
#   and run the whole live test: seeding, a shell job, bin/crons, bin/oh,
#   bin/ask, the keyring across a restart.
# - scripts: shellcheck over bin/, the reconciliation tests, and the hands'
#   unit tests on Python 3.11 (the image's version); none needs a core.
# - web: the Next.js site.
#
# Nothing here deploys. There is no deploy-on-merge: the box runs
# deploy/compose.yaml by hand (deploy/README.md).

name: check

on:
  pull_request:
  workflow_call:

jobs:
  spine:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v5
      # OpenHuman and its nested vendors, all public over https.
      - name: Fetch vendor/openhuman
        run: git submodule update --init --recursive --depth 1 --jobs 8 vendor/openhuman
      # OpenHuman links X11, xdo, evdev and ALSA on Linux.
      - name: Install system headers
        run: |
          sudo apt-get update
          sudo apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends \
            pkg-config libssl-dev libasound2-dev libxdo-dev libxtst-dev \
            libx11-dev libxi-dev libevdev-dev libudev-dev sqlite3
      # Keep in step with rust-toolchain.toml (vendor/openhuman's).
      - uses: dtolnay/rust-toolchain@1.96.1
      - uses: Swatinem/rust-cache@v2
      - run: cargo build --release --locked -p teeny-spine
      - run: bin/test/spine_live_test.sh
        env:
          OPENHUMAN_CORE_BIN: target/release/teeny-spine

  scripts:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v5
      # The hands and bin/lib/*.py: Python 3.11 standard library only (tomllib),
      # so no install step. The tests fake X and the core; nothing leaves the
      # runner.
      - uses: actions/setup-python@v5
        with:
          python-version: "3.11"
      # shellcheck and sqlite3 ship on the runner image.
      - run: shellcheck -x bin/oh bin/ask bin/act bin/doctor bin/eval bin/crons bin/heartbeat bin/spine bin/seed-cron bin/lib/*.sh bin/test/*.sh deploy/*.sh
      - run: bin/test/seed_cron_test.sh
      - run: bin/test/act_test.sh
      - run: bin/test/doctor_test.sh
      - run: bin/test/eval_test.sh
      - run: python3 -m unittest discover -s hands/tests -t hands/tests -v

  web:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    defaults:
      run:
        working-directory: web
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v5
      - uses: actions/setup-node@v5
        with:
          node-version: 22
          cache: npm
          cache-dependency-path: web/package-lock.json
      - run: npm ci
      - run: npm run lint
      - run: npm run build

"""OAuth 1.0a request signing (RFC 5849, HMAC-SHA1), as X signs user-context
calls: every write, `/2/users/me`, and the reads that only the account itself
may make.

The signature covers the method, the URL without its query, the query
parameters, any form-encoded body parameters and the `oauth_*` set. A JSON
body is not a parameter and is not signed, which is what X expects.

Ported from crates/teeny-x/src/oauth.rs.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import base64
import hashlib
import hmac
import itertools
import os
import time
import urllib.parse
from typing import Iterable, Sequence

# RFC 5849 section 3.6: everything but ALPHA, DIGIT, `-`, `.`, `_` and `~`.
_UNRESERVED = "-._~"


def percent_encode(value: str) -> str:
    """Percent-encodes a value the way RFC 5849 requires: UTF-8, upper-case
    hex, and only the unreserved set left alone. (Not `encodeURIComponent`,
    which leaves `!*'()` bare.)"""
    return urllib.parse.quote(value, safe=_UNRESERVED)


class OAuth1:
    """The account's user-context credentials, able to sign a request. Its
    repr names no secret, so a traceback or a log line cannot leak one."""

    __slots__ = ("_consumer_key", "_consumer_secret", "_token", "_token_secret")

    def __init__(self, consumer_key: str, consumer_secret: str, token: str, token_secret: str) -> None:
        self._consumer_key = consumer_key
        self._consumer_secret = [REDACTED]
        self._token = token
        self._token_secret = [REDACTED]

    def __repr__(self) -> str:
        return "OAuth1(<redacted>)"

    __str__ = __repr__

    def header(self, method: str, url: str, form: Sequence[tuple[str, str]] = ()) -> str:
        """The `Authorization` header for one request, with a fresh nonce and
        the current time. `url` carries the query; `form` is a form-encoded
        body, empty for a JSON body or none."""
        return self.header_with(method, url, form, _nonce(), int(time.time()))

    def header_with(
        self, method: str, url: str, form: Sequence[tuple[str, str]], nonce: str, timestamp: int
    ) -> str:
        """`header` with the nonce and timestamp given, so a signature can be
        checked against a known one."""
        base = self.base_string(method, url, form, nonce, timestamp)
        key = f"{percent_encode(self._consumer_secret)}&{percent_encode(self._token_secret)}"
        digest = hmac.new(key.encode(), base.encode(), hashlib.sha1).digest()
        signature = base64.b64encode(digest).decode()
        oauth = sorted([*self._oauth_params(nonce, timestamp), ("oauth_signature", signature)])
        fields = ", ".join(f'{percent_encode(name)}="{percent_encode(value)}"' for name, value in oauth)
        return f"OAuth {fields}"

    def base_string(
        self, method: str, url: str, form: Sequence[tuple[str, str]], nonce: str, timestamp: int
    ) -> str:
        """The signature base string (RFC 5849 section 3.4.1). The query is
        decoded before it is re-encoded, so a value that arrived encoded is
        not encoded twice."""
        parts = urllib.parse.urlsplit(url)
        query = urllib.parse.parse_qsl(parts.query, keep_blank_values=True)
        bare = urllib.parse.urlunsplit((parts.scheme, parts.netloc, parts.path, "", ""))
        params = sorted(
            (percent_encode(name), percent_encode(value))
            for name, value in itertools.chain(query, form, self._oauth_params(nonce, timestamp))
        )
        normalized = "&".join(f"{name}={value}" for name, value in params)
        return f"{method.upper()}&{percent_encode(bare)}&{percent_encode(normalized)}"

    def _oauth_params(self, nonce: str, timestamp: int) -> Iterable[tuple[str, str]]:
        """The `oauth_*` set. A signer with no token (the app alone, asking
        for a request token) sends no `oauth_token` at all, as RFC 5849 has it."""
        params = [
            ("oauth_consumer_key", self._consumer_key),
            ("oauth_nonce", nonce),
            ("oauth_signature_method", "HMAC-SHA1"),
            ("oauth_timestamp", str(timestamp)),
        ]
        if self._token:
            [REDACTED]"oauth_token", self._token))
        params.append(("oauth_version", "1.0"))
        return params


def _nonce() -> str:
    """A nonce only has to be unique per timestamp, not secret, but the OS
    hands out random bytes for free."""
    return os.urandom(16).hex()

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Put teeny.enamakel.com in front of the landing page, once.
#
#   ./deploy/web-vhost.sh          # install the vhost, issue the cert, reload
#
# Two-phase on purpose. The full vhost references a certificate that does not
# exist yet, and certbot's webroot challenge needs nginx already answering for
# the name, so the port 80 block goes in alone first, then the cert is issued,
# then the whole file replaces it. Safe to re-run: certbot keeps an existing
# cert and every other step is idempotent.
#
# Assumes DNS for the name already reaches this box (through Cloudflare or
# not). If it does not, certbot fails at the challenge and nothing is left
# half-installed: the 80-only vhost is harmless and the next run finishes.

set -euo pipefail

REPO_ROOT="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")/.." && pwd)"
cd "$REPO_ROOT"

DEPLOY_HOST="${DEPLOY_HOST:-droid@174.138.35.76}"
DEPLOY_KEY="${DEPLOY_KEY:-$HOME/.ssh/id_rsa}"
DOMAIN="${DOMAIN:-teeny.enamakel.com}"
CONF="deploy/nginx/$DOMAIN.conf"
AVAILABLE="/etc/nginx/sites-available/$DOMAIN.conf"
ENABLED="/etc/nginx/sites-enabled/$DOMAIN.conf"

say() { printf '\n\033[1;35m==>\033[0m %s\n' "$*"; }
die() { printf '\n\033[1;31mfailed:\033[0m %s\n' "$*" >&2; exit 1; }
remote() { ssh -o BatchMode=yes -i "$DEPLOY_KEY" "$DEPLOY_HOST" "$@"; }

[ -f "$CONF" ] || die "no vhost at $CONF"

say "Copying the vhost to the box"
scp -q -i "$DEPLOY_KEY" "$CONF" "$DEPLOY_HOST:/tmp/$DOMAIN.conf"
remote "sudo -n mkdir -p /var/www/certbot"

if remote "sudo -n test -f /etc/letsencrypt/live/$DOMAIN/fullchain.pem"; then
  say "Certificate already exists; installing the full vhost"
else
  say "No certificate yet; installing the port 80 block alone"
  # Everything up to the first 443 server block.
  remote "awk '/listen 443/{exit} {print}' /tmp/$DOMAIN.conf | sed '\$d' | sudo -n tee $AVAILABLE >/dev/null"
  remote "sudo -n ln -sf $AVAILABLE $ENABLED && sudo -n nginx -t && sudo -n systemctl reload nginx" \
    || die "nginx rejected the port 80 vhost"

  say "Issuing the certificate"
  remote "sudo -n certbot certonly --webroot -w /var/www/certbot -d $DOMAIN --non-interactive --agree-tos --keep-until-expiring --register-unsafely-without-email 2>&1 | tail -5" \
    || die "certbot could not issue for $DOMAIN. Does DNS for it reach this box yet? The port 80 vhost is installed; re-run once it does."
fi

remote "sudo -n cp /tmp/$DOMAIN.conf $AVAILABLE && sudo -n ln -sf $AVAILABLE $ENABLED && sudo -n nginx -t && sudo -n systemctl reload nginx" \
  || die "nginx rejected the full vhost"

say "Checking from the box"
remote "curl -sk --max-time 5 -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}\n' -H 'Host: $DOMAIN' https://127.0.0.1/" || true
say "Done. https://$DOMAIN"

"""What the hand returns: plain JSON values, compact, absent fields omitted.

X v2 sends snake_case with everything optional; the step from that to these
shapes is here (crates/teeny-x/src/wire.rs). The shapes are the legacy
`XPost`'s (crates/teeny-x/src/model.rs: camelCase), so rows the old cache
wrote read back unchanged and a model sees what it always saw.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

from dataclasses import dataclass
from typing import Any, Mapping

Json = dict[str, Any]


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class SearchOptions:
    """The knobs on a recent search. Times are ISO 8601, within the last 7
    days. `max_results` is clamped to X's 10..=100 when sent: asking for fewer
    still bills for 10."""

    max_results: int | None = None
    since_id: str | None = None
    start_time: str | None = None
    end_time: str | None = None
    #: `recency` or `relevancy`.
    sort_order: str | None = None
    #: A `nextToken` from an earlier page.
    pagination_token: str | None = None


def _put(target: Json, key: str, value: Any) -> None:
    if value is not None:
        target[key] = value


def _int(value: Any) -> int | None:
    return value if isinstance(value, int) and not isinstance(value, bool) else None


def _metrics(post_id: str, raw: Mapping[str, Any]) -> Json:
    """X's public counters. X has called a repost both things; either spelling
    is read. Impressions are the author's to see, so on somebody else's post
    they are absent."""
    reposts = raw.get("repost_count", raw.get("retweet_count"))
    metrics: Json = {
        "id": post_id,
        "likes": _int(raw.get("like_count")) or 0,
        "replies": _int(raw.get("reply_count")) or 0,
        "reposts": _int(reposts) or 0,
        "quotes": _int(raw.get("quote_count")) or 0,
    }
    _put(metrics, "impressions", _int(raw.get("impression_count")))
    _put(metrics, "bookmarks", _int(raw.get("bookmark_count")))
    return metrics


def to_posts(data: Any, includes: Mapping[str, Any] | None) -> list[Json]:
    """Posts X returned, with authors and attachments joined in from
    `includes`. A post without an id or text is dropped."""
    includes = includes if isinstance(includes, Mapping) else {}
    usernames = {
        user.get("id"): user.get("username")
        for user in includes.get("users") or []
        if isinstance(user, Mapping) and user.get("id") and user.get("username")
    }
    attachments = {
        item.get("media_key"): item
        for item in includes.get("media") or []
        if isinstance(item, Mapping) and item.get("media_key")
    }
    posts: list[Json] = []
    for raw in data if isinstance(data, list) else []:
        if not isinstance(raw, Mapping):
            continue
        post_id, text = raw.get("id"), raw.get("text")
        if not isinstance(post_id, str) or not isinstance(text, str) or not post_id or not text:
            continue
        post: Json = {"id": post_id, "text": text}
        author = raw.get("author_id")
        _put(post, "authorId", author)
        _put(post, "authorUsername", usernames.get(author))
        _put(post, "conversationId", raw.get("conversation_id"))
        _put(post, "createdAt", raw.get("created_at"))
        _put(post, "inReplyToUserId", raw.get("in_reply_to_user_id"))
        media = []
        for key in (raw.get("attachments") or {}).get("media_keys") or []:
            item = attachments.get(key)
            if not item or not item.get("type"):
                continue
            attached: Json = {"type": item["type"]}
            _put(attached, "url", item.get("url"))
            _put(attached, "previewUrl", item.get("preview_image_url"))
            _put(attached, "altText", item.get("alt_text"))
            media.append(attached)
        if media:
            post["media"] = media
        if isinstance(raw.get("public_metrics"), Mapping):
            post["metrics"] = _metrics(post_id, raw["public_metrics"])
        posts.append(post)
    return posts


def to_user(raw: Any, handle: str) -> Json | None:
    """An account looked up by its handle; None when X has no such account
    (suspended, deactivated, never existed)."""
    if not isinstance(raw, Mapping) or not raw.get("id"):
        return None
    metrics = raw.get("public_metrics") if isinstance(raw.get("public_metrics"), Mapping) else {}
    user: Json = {"id": raw["id"], "username": raw.get("username") or handle}
    _put(user, "name", raw.get("name"))
    _put(user, "description", raw.get("description"))
    _put(user, "createdAt", raw.get("created_at"))
    _put(user, "verified", raw.get("verified") if isinstance(raw.get("verified"), bool) else None)
    _put(user, "followers", _int(metrics.get("followers_count")))
    _put(user, "following", _int(metrics.get("following_count")))
    _put(user, "posts", _int(metrics.get("tweet_count")))
    return user


def to_identity(raw: Any, fallback_username: str) -> Json | None:
    """The account the credentials act as, read from the token."""
    if not isinstance(raw, Mapping) or not raw.get("id"):
        return None
    metrics = raw.get("public_metrics") if isinstance(raw.get("public_metrics"), Mapping) else {}
    identity: Json = {"id": raw["id"], "username": raw.get("username") or fallback_username}
    _put(identity, "followers", _int(metrics.get("followers_count")))
    return identity


def utf16_length(text: str) -> int:
    """A post's length as the legacy service measured it: UTF-16 code units
    (JavaScript's `.length`), so an emoji counts two, as X counts it."""
    return len(text.encode("utf-16-le")) // 2

# teeny

Teeny ([`@teenydroid`](https://x.com/teenydroid)) is the TinyHumans mascot. It is a stock
[OpenHuman](https://github.com/tinyhumansai/openhuman) core plus a brain and a
handful of small programs. There is no custom runtime: OpenHuman runs the
agent loop, cron, memory and tools, and Teeny is the files it reads and the
programs it calls.

| | What | Where |
|---|---|---|
| **Spine** | `teeny-spine`, OpenHuman's own command-line host, built here from the vendored library and run as `serve`. It provides the agent loop, model routing, cron, memory (CortexDB), browser, shell and JSON-RPC. No Teeny logic lives in it. | `spine/`, `vendor/openhuman` |
| **Hands** | Small programs that hold every outside capability, every secret and every hard rule. Models only draft; hands act. | `hands/`, `bin/` |
| **Brain** | Who Teeny is and what it does: identity, known facts, skills, narrative, assets and the schedule. All of OpenHuman's state sits beside it in one SQLite file. | `brain/` |

[`docs/architecture.md`](docs/architecture.md) is the design.
[`docs/hands.md`](docs/hands.md) specifies every hand, and
[`docs/oh-gaps.md`](docs/oh-gaps.md) lists what upstream OpenHuman could add to
make the hands smaller.

## How a post happens

```
cron (in the spine) ──► bin/<job> ──► bin/ask  "draft a post"      the model drafts, in Teeny's voice
                                 ──► hands/guard check              lexicon, links, style, model judge
                                 ──► hands/x post                   posting rules, DRY_RUN, X, the ledger
```

Cron runs **shell** jobs, not agent turns. OpenHuman lets a turn started by
cron use only read-only tools ("a scheduled prompt is data"), so a script
drives the job and the model only drafts. The model never sees a key; the
hands read them from `secrets/teeny.env` themselves.

## Status

- **Spine:** done. It builds, boots from `brain/` (in Docker or on a laptop),
  points itself at the model and CortexDB, and seeds cron from
  `brain/cron.toml`.
- **Hands:** `hands/guard` (the content filter) and `hands/x` (reads, post,
  reply, like, upload, unsay) are built and tested.
- **First live run:** the spine booted, the heartbeat ran from cron,
  `bin/ask` drafted a post in Teeny's voice, `hands/guard` passed it, and
  `hands/x post` returned `dry_run: true`.
- **Playbooks:** `bin/act` runs a playbook from `brain/playbooks/` (inputs from
  hand read verbs, a draft from the tool-less `act` agent, the action through
  a hand). `morning` and `mentions` are scheduled but switched off; only
  `heartbeat` runs.
- **Doctor:** `bin/doctor` checks the brain, the crons, the playbooks, the
  invariants, the guard, the storage and the secrets. `bin/spine` won't boot a
  checkout it fails.
- **Evals:** `bin/eval` drafts the frozen tasks in `evals/tasks/` and has the
  tool-less `judge` agent compare two brains pair by pair, blind and twice
  with the order swapped, by the incumbent's soul. The anchors in
  `evals/invariants.md` (never sell $TINY, no buy calls, one token, zero
  toxicity, and more) must hold in every brain.
- **Next:** the self-improvement loop ([`docs/evolve.md`](docs/evolve.md)).
  Teeny edits its own brain, crons included, driven by its lore. A model judges
  each change against the current brain, and a change that wins is merged.
- **`DRY_RUN` is on** until `secrets/teeny.env` says `DRY_RUN=0`.

## Run it

### With Docker (how the box runs it)

```sh
git submodule update --init --recursive vendor/openhuman
mkdir -p secrets && chmod 700 secrets
cp deploy/spine.env.example secrets/spine.env    # the model; CortexDB if wanted
cp deploy/teeny.env.example secrets/teeny.env    # the X keys; DRY_RUN=1
chmod 600 secrets/*.env
TEENY_UID=$(id -u) TEENY_GID=$(id -g) docker compose -f deploy/compose.yaml up -d --build
docker compose -f deploy/compose.yaml logs -f spine      # "[spine] ready" once seeded
```

Run anything below inside the container with
`docker compose -f deploy/compose.yaml exec spine <command>`.
[`deploy/README.md`](deploy/README.md) covers the server: updates, backups and
the landing page.

### On a laptop

```sh
git submodule update --init --recursive vendor/openhuman
cargo build --release -p teeny-spine
bin/spine          # mints secrets/core.token and secrets/openhuman.key on first boot
```

## Operate it

```sh
bin/crons                          # every cron job, its next run and last result (a sqlite query)
bin/crons runs heartbeat           # one job's recent runs
bin/ask "who are you?"             # one agent turn, as Teeny
bin/oh cron_list                   # any JSON-RPC method on the running core
bin/seed-cron --dry-run            # what seeding brain/cron.toml would change
bin/seed-cron --check              # is brain/cron.toml within the cron rules? (no core needed)
bin/act morning                    # run one playbook now (DRY_RUN still applies)
bin/act --check morning            # does it parse?
bin/doctor                         # is this checkout safe to boot? (--live: is the spine healthy?)
bin/eval run state/eval/now        # draft every eval task on the running spine
bin/eval compare A B OUT           # judge two runs; exit 0 when B beats A
bin/eval invariants                # does the brain still say what Teeny is?

hands/x whoami                                        # who the X keys belong to
hands/x search '@teenydroid'                          # a recent search, cached
echo '{"text":"gm"}' | hands/guard check              # ok, or a hold with the reason
echo '{"text":"gm"}' | hands/x post                   # guard, rules, then DRY_RUN or X
hands/guard holds list                                # what the guard is holding for review
```

Every hand prints one JSON object. The exit code is `0` when it's done, `2`
when a rule refused (the JSON says which), and `1` on an error. Add `--help` to
any hand or verb for its flags.

To schedule something, write a playbook in `brain/playbooks/`, add a job that
runs it to `brain/cron.toml`, and restart the spine:

```toml
[jobs.morning]
schedule = "0 7 * * *"
tz = "Asia/Kolkata"
command = "bin/act morning"
```

A brain job runs `bin/heartbeat` or `bin/act <playbook>`. No job may run more
often than every 5 minutes, there can be at most 24 jobs, and `bin/act` can run
at most 400 times a day. The jobs in `evals/cron.pinned.toml` are always added.
These rules live in `bin/lib/cron_policy.py`.

## Configure it

Everything secret lives in `secrets/`. That folder is gitignored and outside
the brain.

**`secrets/spine.env`** (what `bin/spine` gives the core at every boot):

| Key | |
|---|---|
| `LADDER_URL` | Any OpenAI-compatible endpoint, run as OpenHuman's `local-openai` runtime, so no TinyHumans account is needed. |
| `LADDER_API_KEY` | Stored in the core's encrypted store on boot. Can be removed afterwards. |
| `SPINE_MODEL` | The model id every workload uses. |
| `SPINE_CONTEXT_WINDOW` | Optional. Otherwise it's read from the endpoint's `/models`. The core trims prompts to this. |
| `CORTEX_API_URL`, `CORTEX_API_KEY` | Optional memory engine. |

**`secrets/teeny.env`** (read by each hand itself; the process environment
can't override it, though `DRY_RUN=1` in the environment can force a rehearsal):

| Key | |
|---|---|
| `DRY_RUN` | On unless set to `0`. |
| `X_BOT_USERNAME`, `X_API_KEY`, `X_API_SECRET`, `X_ACCESS_TOKEN`, `X_ACCESS_TOKEN_SECRET`, `X_BEARER_TOKEN` | X API v2: OAuth 1.0a for writes, the bearer for reads. |
| `POST_MIN_GAP_HOURS`, `REPLY_MIN_INTERVAL_MS`, `REPLY_MAX_INTERVAL_MS`, ... | The posting rules. See `deploy/teeny.env.example`. |
| `MAX_EMOJI_PER_POST`, `SAFETY_JUDGE`, `LINK_ALLOWLIST` | The guard. |
| `GIPHY_API_KEY` | GIFs for posts. |

The spine writes these itself on first boot: `secrets/core.token` (the RPC
bearer) and `secrets/openhuman.key` (the master key for every secret the core
stores). **Back up `brain/storage.db` and `secrets/openhuman.key` together.**
The database is unreadable without its key.

## Layout

```
spine/               teeny-spine, the one Rust package (OpenHuman's host, built from the library)
vendor/openhuman     upstream tinyhumansai/openhuman, pinned by commit on upstream/main
bin/                 spine, doctor, act, eval, oh, ask, crons, seed-cron, heartbeat; bin/lib/ shared shell and policy; bin/test/
evals/               frozen: what Teeny cannot edit about itself (tasks/, judge.md, invariants.md, cron.pinned.toml)
hands/               guard, x: Python 3.11 stdlib, no dependencies; hands/lib/teeny_hands, hands/tests/
brain/               SOUL.md, CONTEXT.md, skills/, playbooks/, agents/, narrative/ (LORE, ARCS), assets/, calendar.json, cron.toml
deploy/              compose.yaml, spine.env.example, teeny.env.example, the landing page's nginx vhost
web/                 the landing page (Next.js), its own image
docs/                architecture, hands, upstream gaps
```

These are gitignored and created at run time:
- `secrets/`: the env files, the core token and the master key.
- `state/`: what the hands keep. `hands.db` holds the posting ledger, cache,
  holds and pacing, `locks/` the locks, and `core.url` where the core answers.
- `.openhuman/`: the core's config, written by the core.
- `brain/storage.db`: all of the core's state (sessions, cron jobs and runs,
  encrypted secrets) in one SQLite file, so `sqlite3` can read it.
- `brain/IDENTITY.md`, `ROLE.md`, `STYLE.md`: OpenHuman's default persona
  files. It never overwrites Teeny's `SOUL.md`.

## Tests

```sh
python3 -m unittest discover -s hands/tests -t hands/tests   # the hands; X and the core are faked
bin/test/seed_cron_test.sh                                   # cron reconciliation and rules; no core needed
bin/test/act_test.sh                                         # playbooks; the core and hands faked
bin/test/doctor_test.sh                                      # each thing the doctor catches; spine refuses to boot
bin/test/eval_test.sh                                        # hard checks, blind swapped judging, scoring; the core faked
OPENHUMAN_CORE_BIN=target/release/teeny-spine bin/test/spine_live_test.sh
```

The live test boots a real spine over a scratch copy of the checkout, against
a stub model. It checks:
- first-boot minting and the file keyring;
- the single storage file, and that `SOUL.md` is left alone;
- cron seeding and a shell job running;
- `bin/crons`, `bin/oh` and `bin/ask`, and that the model receives the
  question it was asked;
- the model's context window;
- the doctor passing at boot, and `bin/doctor --live` on the running spine;
- `bin/act` running a playbook, with the `act` agent offering the model no tools;
- `bin/eval` drafting a task and judging a pair, with the `judge` agent offering
  the model no tools;
- the key surviving a restart.

CI (`.github/workflows/check.yml`) builds the spine and runs every test above, plus
shellcheck and the landing page's checks.

## Bumping OpenHuman

1. Move `vendor/openhuman` to the new `upstream/main` commit and run
   `git submodule update --init --recursive vendor/openhuman`.
2. Re-copy its root `[patch]` tables into `Cargo.toml`, with paths rebased
   onto `vendor/openhuman/`. Drop any entry that `cargo metadata` warns "was
   not used in the crate graph". Cargo records those in `Cargo.lock` in an
   order that differs between macOS and Linux, which breaks the image's
   `--locked` build.
3. Run `cargo build --release -p teeny-spine`.
4. Run the live test against the new binary.

# teeny / mind

The landing page for Teeny's mind: its soul, the rules it runs under, the tools
it can reach, how its memory works, a log of reflections behind each reply, and
the mistakes it made in public.

Next.js 16, Tailwind v4, shadcn/ui (Base UI primitives), three.js via
react-three-fiber.

## Pages

One route per part of the mind, each with its own scene behind the hero:

| Route | What | Scene |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `/` | the token counter, both minds; the agents' desk; the last few calls | a brain: points on a sphere, linked to their neighbours, neurons firing |
| `/ledger` | every model call: input, thinking, output, cost, digest; the journal's turns; the lessons | a stream of thoughts flowing past a few that settled |
| `/brain` | the OpenCompany company: the desk, the roster, the workflow, the runs, the repository | rings of tools orbiting a core |
| `/soul` | who it is | one warm, soft, restless blob |
| `/rules` | what no message can change | a core held inside a cage of turning rings |
| `/tools` | everything it can do, and cannot | a lattice of points |

`/reflections`, `/memory` and `/lessons` are gone: the ledger is where the
turns and the lessons live now, and memory is described under the rules.

`src/lib/pages.ts` is the registry: nav, home cards, heroes and prev/next all
read from it. Scenes live in `src/components/scene/scenes/` and honour
`prefers-reduced-motion` by standing still.

```sh
npm install
npm run dev      # http://localhost:3000
npm run build
```

## The feeds

Set `MIND_API_URL` to the bot's base URL and the page reads three things from
it, each revalidated every 60s and marked live: `/mind` (the journal:
`src/lib/mind.ts`), `/ledger` (every model call and the running token count:
`src/lib/ledger.ts`) and `/brain` (the roster, the workflows and the latest
runs of the OpenCompany company: `src/lib/company.ts`). Unset or unreachable,
every page says so and shows nothing: there is no sample data anywhere. `BRAIN_REPO` (default `teenydroid/brain`) is read from the
public GitHub API for the commits shown on `/brain`; `GITHUB_TOKEN` is optional
and only raises the rate limit.

The counter on the front page is one figure, every token Teeny has burned
across the account and the brain, counting from the first call the ledger
saw. It polls `/api/pulse`, a route in this app that reads the bot's totals
on every request, every twenty seconds, and rolls to the new value. It never
extrapolates: between polls it holds still.

The desk (`src/components/agent-desk.tsx`) lays the brain's workflow out by
rank and replays its latest run from the host's own step record; with no run
recorded yet it rehearses the workflow from its node summaries and says so.
Everything static on the page (`src/lib/brain.ts`) is sourced from `SOUL.md`,
`CONTEXT.md`, `README.md` and the published tool list.

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Tests for bin/doctor, and for bin/spine refusing to boot a checkout the
# doctor fails. Each case breaks one thing in a scratch copy of the checkout.
# No OpenHuman needed: the spine is handed a stand-in core that only records
# that it was started.
#
#   bin/test/doctor_test.sh
set -euo pipefail

here="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"
repo="$(cd "$here/../.." && pwd)"
scratch="$(mktemp -d "${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/teeny-doctor.XXXXXX")"
trap 'rm -rf "$scratch"' EXIT

failures=0
pass() { printf 'ok   %s\n' "$1"; }
fail() { printf 'FAIL %s\n' "$1" >&2; failures=$((failures + 1)); }
check() { local name="$1"; shift; if "$@"; then pass "$name"; else fail "$name"; fi; }

unset OPENHUMAN_CORE_TOKEN OPENHUMAN_CORE_URL OPENHUMAN_WORKSPACE CALENDAR_TZ \
  TEENY_ROOT TEENY_BRAIN TEENY_STORAGE TEENY_SECRETS TEENY_STATE TEENY_HANDS

# A fresh copy of what the box runs: bin/, hands/, evals/ and the brain.
root="$scratch/root"
fresh() {
  rm -rf "$root"
  mkdir -p "$root/brain"
  cp -R "$repo/bin" "$repo/evals" "$root/"
  mkdir -p "$root/hands"
  cp -R "$repo/hands/lib" "$repo/hands/x" "$repo/hands/guard" "$root/hands/"
  cp -R "$repo/brain/playbooks" "$repo/brain/agents" "$repo/brain/narrative" "$root/brain/"
  cp "$repo/brain/SOUL.md" "$repo/brain/CONTEXT.md" "$repo/brain/cron.toml" "$root/brain/"
}
doctor() { "$root/bin/doctor" >"$scratch/report.json" 2>"$scratch/doctor.log"; }
fails() { # NAME CHECK-SUBSTRING: the doctor exits 1 and names the failing check
  local name="$1" what="$2"
  if doctor; then
    fail "$name (the doctor passed)"
  elif grep -q "^FAIL $what" "$scratch/doctor.log"; then
    pass "$name"
  else
    fail "$name (failed for something else: $(grep '^FAIL' "$scratch/doctor.log" | head -2 | tr '\n' ' '))"
  fi
}

# --- a healthy checkout ------------------------------------------------------------
fresh
check "passes a fresh copy of the checkout" doctor
check "writes its report to state/doctor.json" test "$(jq -r .ok "$root/state/doctor.json")" = true
check "prints the same report" test "$(jq -r .ok "$scratch/report.json")" = true
check "checks every scheduled playbook" grep -q '^ok   playbook morning' "$scratch/doctor.log"
check "checks the guard's screen" grep -q '^ok   guard screen' "$scratch/doctor.log"

fails "fails without SOUL.md" "brain/SOUL.md"

fails "fails on an empty CONTEXT.md" "brain/CONTEXT.md"

fails "fails a cron naming a playbook that does not exist" "cron.toml"

fails "fails a playbook nothing schedules yet" "playbook someday"
fresh; sed -i.bak 's/^named = \[\]/named = ["shell"]/' "$root/brain/agents/act.toml"
fails "fails an act agent that was given a tool" "agent act.toml"
fresh; rm "$root/brain/agents/act.toml"

fresh; sed -i.bak 's/^named = \[\]/named = ["shell"]/' "$root/brain/agents/judge.toml"

fresh; sqlite3 "$root/brain/storage.db" 'create table t (x); insert into t values (1);'
fails "fails a storage.db without its master key" "secrets/openhuman.key"
mkdir -p "$root/secrets"; (umask 077 && echo key >"$root/secrets/openhuman.key")
check "passes a storage.db with its key" doctor
check "and checks the database itself" grep -q '^ok   storage.db: quick_check ok' "$scratch/doctor.log"
chmod 644 "$root/secrets/openhuman.key"
fails "fails a master key other users can read" "secrets/openhuman.key mode"
chmod 600 "$root/secrets/openhuman.key"
printf 'this is not a database, it is %0500d' 0 >"$root/brain/storage.db"
fails "fails a storage.db that is not a database" "storage.db"

# --- bin/spine will not boot what the doctor fails -----------------------------------------
cat >"$scratch/fake-core" <<'FAKE'
#!/usr/bin/env bash
echo started >>"$FAKE_CORE_LOG"
exit 0
FAKE
chmod +x "$scratch/fake-core"
fresh
printf '[jobs.x]\nschedule = "* * * * *"\ncommand = "bin/heartbeat"\n' >"$root/brain/cron.toml"
: >"$scratch/core.log"
if FAKE_CORE_LOG="$scratch/core.log" OPENHUMAN_CORE_BIN="$scratch/fake-core" OPENHUMAN_CORE_PORT=1 \
  "$root/bin/spine" >"$scratch/spine.log" 2>&1; then
  fail "bin/spine refuses to boot a checkout the doctor fails"
else
  check "bin/spine refuses to boot a checkout the doctor fails" grep -q 'bin/doctor failed' "$scratch/spine.log"
fi
check "and never starts the core" test ! -s "$scratch/core.log"
check "and leaves the reason in state/doctor.json" test "$(jq -r '.checks[] | select(.status == "fail") | .check' "$root/state/doctor.json")" = cron.toml

if [ "$failures" -gt 0 ]; then
  printf '%d failure(s)\n' "$failures" >&2
  exit 1
fi
echo "all passed"
